summary: bound.PageOptions/mcpPageConfig carry a FirstPageOnlyFields list; workouts_list sets it to ["summary"]. A named field is kept only on a query's very first page (no incoming cursor) and dropped from every later page, so workouts_list's per-month workout histogram (confirmed live at ~1.5 KB) stops being repeated fixed overhead on every page a caller pages through -- but only for the unprojected default response. mcpToolPageResultText computes the top-level names actually present in the call's "select" (topLevelSelectFieldNames) and passes them as bound.PageOptions.KeepFirstPageOnlyFields; only a FirstPageOnlyFields entry whose name appears there survives on a later page -- select=data.id,summary keeps summary, select=id still strips it, and no select at all strips it too. A regen touching workouts_list's mcpPageConfig, mcpToolPageResultText, or topLevelSelectFieldNames must keep all three in agreement.
reason: Live retesting found summary present unchanged on every cursor page of workouts_list, useful once on page 1 and pure repeated cost afterward -- flagged as an easy byte win on the one endpoint (workouts) whose sync/archive path is still unexercised in live testing. A Greptile review on the resulting PR then found the first implementation stripped summary unconditionally on later pages, including when a caller explicitly select'd it -- silently returning less than requested. A second Greptile review found that fix over-corrected: disabling the strip for ANY select (not just one naming summary) let summary leak through on a later page for a select that never asked for it (e.g. select=id), since select's own envelope fallback can pass unselected sibling metadata through unfiltered.
validated_outcome: go build/vet/test/verify_skill.py all green. TestEndpointPageResponseFirstPageOnlyFieldsDroppedOnLaterPages drives a first-page/second-page pair through the real EndpointPageResponse call path and asserts summary present on page one, absent on page two, with other fields (total) unaffected on both. TestMCPToolPageResultTextRespectsExplicitSelectOfFirstPageOnlyField (updated after the second Greptile finding) now checks three cases on a resumed call: select naming summary keeps it, select naming only a sibling field (id) still drops it, and no select at all still drops it.
